product.olivetti-m250e.summary: Separate 12 MHz M250-family 80286 board with 82C206 logic and its own firmware identity.
product.olivetti-m250e.history: The M250 E is documented alongside the M250 in Olivetti service material, but has distinct 12 MHz timing, CHIPS 82C206 and GA80/GA99 board logic, as well as its own PDSF/PDSD firmware. Its Setup documents 20, 40 and 100 MB Conner types, while a standalone sales configuration and release date remain unrecovered.
product.olivetti-m250e.warning: IN DEVELOPMENT: we are working on the M250 E emulation. You can create the machine, but it may fail or stop partway. Any result you send us, even if it does not boot, helps us finish it.
product.olivetti-m250e.creation.model: Documented technical identity: 12 MHz 80286 M250 E board with 82C206 and separate PDSF/PDSD firmware
product.olivetti-m250e.creation.note: The optional hard disk is one of the Conner drives in Olivetti's table, on the on-board IDE interface; choose the same type in Setup. Type 7 (CP3044) is not offered because it arrived with BIOS 1.07 and the preserved BIOS is 1.06.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.market: Late-1980s M250-family derivative. Its standalone commercial positioning, release date and regional bundles remain pending.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.commerc: The service guide documents the 12 MHz board, 2 or 4 MB of memory and the Conner drives in Setup: CP3022 20 MB, CP346 and CP3142 40 MB, CP3106 100 MB and, from BIOS 1.07, CP3044 40 MB. No list of sales configurations has been found.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz, documented separately from M250's 8 MHz design.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.memory: Service material documents 2 MB using two 512 KB SIMMs and 4 MB using two 512 KB plus two 1 MB SIMMs. The 1 MB default is a current emulation profile, not a claimed sales configuration.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.chipset: CHIPS 82C206 peripheral controller with GA80/GA99 logic and an M250 E-only port at 6Bh. BluMach currently uses the shared AT peripheral path where 82C206-specific behavior is not documented.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.storage: On-board AT disk interface at 1F0h-1F7h and IRQ 14, which Olivetti calls the AT/RLL adapter; it is the same IDE interface as on the M250. Setup types in BIOS 1.06: 1, CP346 40 MB (805/4/26); 2, CP3106 100 MB (776/8/33); 3, CP3142 40 MB (635/4/33); 4, CP3022 20 MB (615/4/17); 5, 745/4/28, and 6, 965/5/17, with no identified drive. The service guide gives 766 cylinders for type 2, but the BIOS has 776. BIOS 1.07 adds type 7 for the CP3044. P6 selects 1:1 or 1:3 interleave and P10 states whether a disk is fitted; the BIOS takes the disk from CMOS.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.jumpers: P1/P2 choose 1, 2 or 4 MB of RAM. P6 selects the disk interleave, P8 the battery, P9 the floppy mode (16 MHz or 1.2 MB), P10 disk presence, P11 the serial port, P12 VGA and P15/P20 hysteresis and precompensation. BluMach does not model them.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.firmwar: Observed local sets are PDSF 1.06 system BIOS and PDSD 1.06 PVGA1A video BIOS. They are distinct from M250 firmware and remain local-only.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.verifie: Local isolated cold initialization at 12 MHz/1 MB created NVR without a ROM-load error. It is not visual POST or diagnostic evidence.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.limitat: On-screen POST, Setup and System Test, soft reset, RTC, operating system, hard disk and the documented memory sizes are still missing. Its PDSD 1.06 video BIOS is now loaded at C0000h; until this version the Amstrad video ROM was loaded. The 82C206 and jumpers P6, P9 and P10 are documented hardware differences that the emulation does not yet reproduce in a verified way.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.service: Olivetti Pocket Service Guide, M250 E board, memory and controller sections
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.brochur: M250 1989 brochure retained as family context only; not proof of an M250 E commercial bundle
No hard disk: one 1.44 MB floppy drive
